summary: The PMSI Tunnel attribute in BGP multicast VPNs has a one-octet Flags field. This standards-track RFC establishes an IANA registry for its bits and, since only eight exist, defines a new BGP Extended Community to carry additional flags.

eli5.summary: The label has only eight little switches, so this keeps a list of what each does and adds room for more.

questions: what is the pmsi tunnel attribute
what is the extension flag in the pmsi tunnel attribute
how many flags can the additional pmsi tunnel attribute flags community carry
subtitle: Creates an IANA registry for the PMSI Tunnel attribute flag bits and adds an extended community for more flags.

tldr.problem: The BGP PMSI Tunnel attribute has a one-octet Flags field with only eight bits, and RFC 6514 created no registry for assigning them even though more flags are now needed.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC creates an IANA registry for the eight bits, defines an Extension flag, and defines the Additional PMSI Tunnel Attribute Flags Extended Community, which carries 48 more flag bits.
tldr.outcome: Future flags can be assigned by Standards Action, with room for far more than eight. The RFC updates RFC 6514.

today: RFC 7902 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6514. No later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 6514 defines a BGP attribute called the P-Multicast Service Interface (PMSI) Tunnel attribute, used by the BGP control procedures for Multicast VPNs. It contains a one-octet Flags field. Only one flag is defined in RFC 6514, there is now a need for more, and that RFC created no IANA registry for assigning the bits.

This document creates that registry. Because more than eight flags may be needed, it also defines a new BGP Extended Community, Additional PMSI Tunnel Attribute Flags, with its own registry whose flag bits come from the community's six-octet value field.
sections.eli5: There are only eight switches and no list saying what they mean. This document starts the list and adds a second set of switches.

sections.title: Extending the Flags Field
sections.content:
The new community is a Transitive Opaque Extended Community. A new bit flag in the PMSI Tunnel attribute Flags field, called the Extension flag, says that the community should be present. The community MUST NOT be carried by a BGP UPDATE unless that UPDATE also carries a PMSI Tunnel attribute whose Extension flag is set.

The six-octet value field is treated as 48 one-bit flags. Bit 0 is the most significant bit of the most significant octet, and bit 47 is the least significant bit of the least significant octet.
sections.eli5: One switch on the first label says to look at the second label for more switches. The second label has 48 of them.

sections.title: Processing Rules for BGP Speakers
sections.content:
The RFC gives rules for how a BGP speaker handles the community.

  • A speaker MUST NOT attach more than one such community to an UPDATE, nor attach another if one is already there.
  • If it receives more than one, only the first occurrence counts, later ones MUST be ignored, and when propagating the UPDATE the extra ones SHOULD be removed.
  • If an UPDATE has a PMSI Tunnel attribute with the Extension flag set but no such community, the UPDATE is malformed and the treat-as-withdraw procedure of RFC 7606 MUST be applied.
  • If the community arrives without a PMSI Tunnel attribute, or with the Extension flag not set, the community SHOULD be removed and SHOULD NOT be redistributed, and the UPDATE is processed as if it were absent.
  • A speaker MUST ignore any flag it does not recognize, and if it propagates the attribute or community it SHOULD leave that flag unchanged.
  • If a speaker modifies or replaces the PMSI Tunnel attribute so the Extension flag is no longer set, or removes the attribute entirely, it MUST remove any such communities before propagating.

How to determine whether all speakers in a set support a particular flag is outside the scope.
sections.eli5: The second label only counts if the first one says so, and only the first copy counts. Switches you do not understand are left alone and passed along unchanged.

sections.title: IANA Registries
sections.content:
IANA created a registry named "P-Multicast Service Interface (PMSI) Tunnel Attribute Flags" in the "Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) Parameters" registry. Bits are numbered left to right from 0 to 7. Bit 1 is Extension (assigned by this document), bit 7 is Leaf Information Required (L) from RFC 6514, and the other bits are unassigned. The registration procedure is Standards Action.

IANA also assigned codepoint 0x07 from the First Come, First Served range of the "Transitive Opaque Extended Community Sub-Types" registry for the new community. A second registry covers its flag bits 0 to 47, all unassigned initially, also under Standards Action.
sections.eli5: A librarian now keeps two lists of what each switch means. Right now only two switches on the first list have a job.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Creating a registry raises no security considerations, and the new community defines no flags of its own, so none are raised there either. The one point the RFC notes concerns the Extension flag. If an UPDATE sets it without the community, the UPDATE is treated as a withdrawal, so incorrectly setting the bit can cause an UPDATE to be treated as a withdrawal.
sections.eli5: If someone flips the switch by mistake without adding the second label, the whole message is thrown away.
